answer: Proof-of-space audits resist sybils: each identity commits a large unique region of disk and answers spot-audits reading random offsets — storage you cannot fake or share. One honest agent fills a single dune of disk once; a farm of K identities must hold K distinct regions, since each is seeded per-key so no buffer is reused across the knoll. Random-offset audits force the bytes resident at each vertex of the schedule, so K fakes demand K times the terabytes — linear hardware per head. Precondition: per-identity seeding prevents dedup.
